selection: Reservoirs that publish a daily surface elevation beside their storage (ADR-135). An entry names the published reservoir by its source_station_id, the provider's elevation item, the vertical datum the level is measured above, the evidence for that datum with the date it was checked, the measured difference to the other datum a reader is likely to meet, and any reference levels with the authority that set them. Reclamation's RISE service does not label a datum on its elevation items and is not one datum throughout (Taylor Park, item 796, matches the Geological Survey's NAVD 1988 series), so every entry carries its own datum evidence and none is assumed from the provider. An operator's own project datum is entered as vertical_datum project, with its name and its stated relation to a national datum (the feet to add, the operator's words and an HTTPS source).

datum_evidence.summary: No Reclamation page names the datum, and the RISE item's verticalDatum field is null. Over 91 days, 2026-07-28 to 2026-10-26, RISE item 508 minus USGS 09379900 parameter 62614 (NGVD 1929) had a median of +0.14 ft (the instantaneous reading nearest local midnight) and +0.21 ft (the daily mean); RISE minus parameter 62615 (NAVD 1988) had a median of -2.76 ft. Larger gaps fall only on fast-rising days, where an end-of-day value and a daily mean differ in time. USGS SIR 2022-5017, written with Reclamation, gives full pool as 3,702.91 ft above NAVD 88 against Reclamation's 3,700 ft, an offset of about 2.9 ft consistent with NGVD 1929.

record_starts.basis: End of first filling. Readings from the closure of the dam in 1963 to this date describe the lake filling, not its operation, and are left out of the record readings and the history rank; they stay in the daily history.
record_starts.quote: Lake Powell began filling on March 13, 1963 and completed filling on June 22, 1980 reaching elevation 3,700 feet above sea level

datum_relation.quote: Elevation of reservoir water surface. Tied to 'Power House' datum. Add 0.55 feet to convert to NGVD29, from leveling of 1935.

datum_evidence.summary: Reclamation's 2001 Lake Mead Sedimentation Survey (Ferrari, February 2008) states: 'All elevation data were tied to the Hoover Dam powerhouse datum that is 0.55 feet lower than NGVD29 (Lara and Sanders, 1970)', and of the reservoir water surface: 'Add 0.55 feet to convert to NGVD29, from leveling of 1935.' That RISE item 6123 is on this datum is an inference from Reclamation's own reports that its stage data are tied to it, not a measurement: no active U.S. Geological Survey elevation series exists to compare (09421000 carried storage only and ended 2017-09-30). RISE's verticalDatum field is null. Owner decision to publish on this basis: 2026-10-27.

sources.citation: Bureau of Reclamation, 2001 Lake Mead Sedimentation Survey (Ferrari, February 2008)
Bureau of Reclamation RISE, catalog item 6123, Lake Mead daily lake/reservoir elevation

derived_offset.basis: Calculated, not measured at the lake: NAVD 88 minus NGVD 29 is 2.35 ft at National Geodetic Survey benchmark GR0577 (1,234.87 ft against 1,232.52 ft) and 2.34 ft at GR0578 (1,234.91 against 1,232.57), both on the Hoover Dam crest; adding the 0.55 ft between the powerhouse datum and NGVD 29 gives about 2.9 ft.

record_starts.basis: The first date Reclamation reports the lake at its spillway, which this site takes as the end of first filling. Readings from the closure of the dam in 1935 to this date are left out of the record readings and the history rank; they stay in the daily history.
record_starts.quote: On August 6 of 1941, Lake Mead’s water level was within one-foot of the spillway crest when the Arizona spillway gates were lowered allowing flows for the first time.
